value.description: The man who argues with Asha, sits down angrily, and later tells Rosa her services will no longer be needed.
evidence: "Mr. Serrano. Sit down."
Daniel sat down.
"Mr. Serrano informed me last Friday that my services would not be required after the funeral."

value.description: The authoritative speaker who questions Rosa about the paper and directs Daniel to sit down.
evidence: "Mr. Serrano. Sit down."
"Rosa," Asha said. "What did the paper say."
Asha had used the voice she had been taught

value.description: The former employee who explains the paper, the will change, the signing, and where the folder was stored.
evidence: "Rosa," Asha said. "What did the paper say."
"I did not read it carefully."
"No."
"Because it is not my house," Rosa said

value.description: The deceased woman whose will, papers, sewing room, and desk drawer are discussed.

"The señora put the paper in a folder"
"Have you looked for the folder since she died?"

value.description: The neighbor who signed the document with the señora and Rosa.
evidence: "Mrs. Kim from across the street signed."

value.description: The lawyer named as not being the one on the telephone during the document signing.
evidence: "The lawyer, not Mr. Halloran but another man, was on the telephone."

value.description: The person who asked Rosa to come to the meeting.

value.description: The judge referenced by Asha as the source of her courtroom authority.
